blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets on your Mac

Google Sheets does not have a native Mac application. You can create a shortcut that behaves like an app. Open Chrome and navigate to your sheet. Click the three-dot menu at the top right. Select Cast, Save, and Share, then choose Install page as app. This creates a dedicated window for your governance work.

Data governance relies on clear lineage. Use separate tabs for raw data, processed data, and final reports. Label your columns clearly. Use Data Validation to restrict inputs to specific formats or lists. This prevents bad data from entering your governance logs.

items: Use conditional formatting to highlight cells that fail validation rules.
Add a metadata tab to document the source of every data column.
Use the Revision History to track who changed specific governance policies.
Lock sensitive cells to prevent accidental edits by other team members.

blocks.text: Speed is important when you have hundreds of rows to audit. Press ⌘ + / to see the full list of shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to find and replace outdated data definitions. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide rows that do not require current attention.

Google Sheets now supports up to 20 million cells. Large sheets can become slow. Break your data into smaller files if you notice lag. Link files using the IMPORTRANGE function to maintain a connection between your master governance file and individual data reports.

items: Relying on manual data entry instead of automated imports.
Sharing files with edit access when only view access is needed.
Ignoring the Revision History until a major error occurs.
Using complex formulas without documenting them in a separate sheet.

blocks.text: Governance is a team effort. Use comments to discuss data quality issues directly in the sheet. Mention colleagues using @ to notify them. Always set clear permissions before sharing a document to ensure compliance with your security policies.

Lazur helps you stay focused on your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about spreadsheet features. Ask Lazur to guide you through setting up complex data validation rules. Use the dictation feature to record meeting notes about data policy changes without leaving your spreadsheet window.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, there is no official native Mac app. You can create a Progressive Web App shortcut in Chrome for a dedicated window.

faq.question: How can I improve my data governance in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Use data validation, maintain clear documentation tabs, and regularly audit your sheets using the Revision History.

faq.question: What is the cell limit for Google Sheets?
faq.answer: As of September 2026, the maximum capacity for a single spreadsheet is 20 million cells.
